s0003.literal: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu
s0003.idiomatic: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu

s0004.literal: Wang Chong, styled Changshen, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
s0004.idiomatic: Wang Chong, styled Changshen, was a native of Linyi in Langye.

s0005.literal: His grandfather Sengyan was Palace Attendant of Qi.
s0005.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengyan had been palace attendant of Qi.

s0006.literal: His father Maozhang was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate in Liang.
s0006.idiomatic: His father Maozhang was an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate under Liang.

s0007.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in Qi times, and the Emperor, because Chong was a lone orphan, cherished him deeply.
s0007.idiomatic: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, finding Chong a fatherless child, doted on him.

s0008.literal: At eighteen he began his career as Secretary of Liang.
s0008.idiomatic: At eighteen he entered service as a secretary of Liang.

s0009.literal: Soon he became Administrator of Yongjia.
s0009.idiomatic: He was soon made administrator of Yongjia.

s0010.literal: He entered court as Mentor to the Heir Apparent and left office on his father's death.
s0010.idiomatic: He returned to court as mentor to the heir apparent and resigned when his father died.

s0011.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed External Military Aide on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan in the Grand Marshal's office and Leader of Direct Service in the Eastern Palace.
s0011.idiomatic: After mourning he was named external military aide on the Prince of Linchuan's staff in the Grand Marshal's office and leader of direct service in the eastern palace.

s0012.literal: He rose through Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
s0012.idiomatic: He rose to be grand mentor to the heir apparent and attendant to the heir apparent.

s0013.literal: He went out as General Who Recruits the Distant and Interior Magistrate of Hengyang.
s0013.idiomatic: He was posted as General Who Recruits the Distant and interior magistrate of Hengyang.

s0014.literal: He was transferred to General of Martial Prestige, Chief Clerk to the Heir of the Princedom of Ancheng, and Interior Magistrate of Changsha, his rank as general unchanged.
s0014.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of Martial Prestige, chief clerk to the heir of Ancheng, and interior magistrate of Changsha, retaining his general's title.

s0015.literal: When the prince died in Xiangzhou, Chong was left to oversee Xiangzhou affairs.
s0015.idiomatic: When the prince died at Xiangzhou, Chong was left to govern the province.

s0016.literal: He entered court as Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent.
s0016.idiomatic: He returned to court as household supporter of the heir apparent.

s0017.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
s0017.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

s0018.literal: In the third year of Datong, as the emperor's sister's son he was enfeoffed Marquis of Andong ting, Editorial footnote marker 1. with a fief of one hundred fifty households.
s0018.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong (537), as kin of the imperial house he was made Marquis of Andong, [1] with a fief of one hundred fifty households.

s0019.literal: He served as General of Manifest Prestige, Administrator of Nan commandery, Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent, and Palace Attendant.
s0019.idiomatic: He held the posts of General of Manifest Prestige, administrator of Nan commandery, household supporter of the heir apparent, and palace attendant.

s0020.literal: He went out to oversee Wu commandery; when his term ended he received the actual appointment.
s0020.idiomatic: He was sent to oversee Wu commandery and, when his term ended, received the substantive appointment.

s0021.literal: He was summoned as Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, concurrently Master of the Left for the People.
s0021.idiomatic: He was recalled as regular attendant of the Secretariat and made concurrent master of the left for the people.

s0022.literal: He went out as General of Manifest Prestige, Chief Clerk to the Prince of Dangyang, Administrator of Jiangxia, conducting office in Yingzhou.
s0022.idiomatic: He went out as General of Manifest Prestige, chief clerk to the Prince of Dangyang, administrator of Jiangxia, and acting governor of Yingzhou.

s0023.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General Who Pacifies the West.
s0023.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Shaoling, General Who Pacifies the West.

s0024.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Luling, Grand General of Cavalry, and Administrator of Nan commandery.
s0024.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Luling, grand general of cavalry, and administrator of Nan commandery.

s0025.literal: When the prince died, he conducted the prefecture and princely establishment affairs.
s0025.idiomatic: When the prince died, he ran the prefecture and the princely establishment.

s0026.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang held Jingzhou, he was Chief Clerk to the Establishment Pacifying the West, general and administrator unchanged.
s0026.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang held Jingzhou, he became chief clerk to the establishment pacifying the west, keeping his general's title and his post as administrator.

s0027.literal: Chong's nature was gentle and compliant; in serving superiors he was reverent; versed in statutes, his governance fair and orderly; as aide in two princely establishments he rarely failed in virtue; though he won no brilliant renown, over time men came to miss him—thus he was esteemed and repeatedly held office at the two-thousand-shi level.
s0027.idiomatic: Chong was mild and obliging, reverent toward his superiors, and skilled in law; his rule was even-handed. Twice he served as an aide to princely establishments and scarcely stained his name. He won no dazzling fame, yet men remembered him long after—so he was held in esteem and repeatedly held governorships.

s0028.literal: He also understood music, was skilled in song and dance, and good at friendship; among the noble wanderers his fame was very great.
s0028.idiomatic: He also knew music, excelled at song and dance, and made friends easily; among the great families his name rang far.

s0029.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan of Liang at Jingzhou assumed the provisional regime; Chong asked to be relieved of Nan commandery to yield it to Wang Sengbian, and also presented ten female entertainers as military reward.
s0029.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, when Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the provisional regime at Jingzhou, Chong asked to give up Nan commandery for Wang Sengbian and sent ten female entertainers as a gift toward the army's expenses.

s0030.literal: Yuan appointed him Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs over the four prefectures Heng, Gui, Cheng, and He, General of the Clouded Pennon, and Inspector of Hengzhou.
s0030.idiomatic: Yuan made him bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs over Heng, Gui, Cheng, and He, General of the Clouded Pennon, and inspector of Hengzhou.

s0031.literal: Yuan's fourth son Yuanliang was Inspector of Xiangzhou; Chong again conducted the province, concurrently Interior Magistrate of Changsha.
s0031.idiomatic: Yuan's fourth son Yuanliang was inspector of Xiangzhou; Chong again governed the province while serving as interior magistrate of Changsha.

s0032.literal: When Jing was pacified, he was appointed General Who Assists the Left and Intendant of Danyang.
s0032.idiomatic: After Jing was suppressed, he was made General Who Assists the Left and intendant of Danyang.

s0033.literal: When the Prince of Wuling raised troops to the gorge mouth, Wang Lin's lieutenant Lu Na and others held Xiangzhou in response; Chong was detained by Na.
s0033.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling marched to the gorge mouth, Wang Lin's lieutenant Lu Na and others seized Xiangzhou in support; Chong was held by Na.

s0034.literal: When Na surrendered, Chong was again appointed Palace Attendant and General of Central Authority, with aides and clerks as needed, Intendant unchanged.
s0034.idiomatic: When Na surrendered, Chong was again made palace attendant and General of Central Authority, with aides and clerks as needed, and kept the intendant's post.

s0035.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing of Liang as Grand Preceptor assumed the provisional regime and made Chong left chief clerk.
s0035.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing of Liang, acting as grand preceptor under the provisional regime, made Chong his left chief clerk.

s0036.literal: In the Shaotai era he rose through Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the right.
s0036.idiomatic: In the Shaotai era he rose from left grand master of the golden sigil to right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

s0037.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director, Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant and general unchanged.
s0037.idiomatic: He was made left vice director and opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, retaining palace attendant and his general's title.

s0038.literal: Soon he again headed Danyang as Intendant and Grand Arbiter of South Xuzhou, with support staff granted.
s0038.idiomatic: Soon he again headed Danyang as intendant and served as grand arbiter of South Xuzhou, with aides granted to support him.

s0039.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was relieved as Intendant; in his former office he headed Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil.
s0039.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, he left the intendant's post and, in his former rank, headed the left grand master of the golden sigil.

s0040.literal: Before he took up the appointment, he was changed to head Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
s0040.idiomatic: Before he entered that office he was reassigned to head tutor to the heir apparent.

s0041.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was relieved as Junior Tutor and given Supernumerary Privilege and Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil.
s0041.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he was relieved as junior tutor and given supernumerary privilege together with the left grand master of the golden sigil.

s0042.literal: Soon in his former office he again headed Danyang as Intendant and joined in compiling statutes and ordinances.
s0042.idiomatic: Soon, in his former capacity, he again headed Danyang as intendant and took part in compiling statutes and ordinances.

s0043.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was given ten trusted attendants.
s0043.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, he was granted ten trusted attendants.

s0044.literal: At first the Founder, because Chong was an old minister of the previous dynasty, specially showed him the respect due elder and younger.
s0044.idiomatic: At first the Founder, treating Chong as a veteran of the old court, paid him the special courtesy owed between elder and younger.

s0045.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, respect increased; once he followed Emperor Wen on a visit to Minister of Works Xu Du's residence, and at the banquet the Emperor gave him an armrest.
s0045.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, the honor grew; once, accompanying the emperor to Minister of Works Xu Du's house, he was given an armrest at the banquet.

s0046.literal: Such was the honor shown him.
s0046.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

s0047.literal: In the first year of Guangda he died, aged seventy-six.
s0047.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangda (567) he died, aged seventy-six.

s0048.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works, posthumous name Yuancian.
s0048.idiomatic: He was posthumously made palace attendant and minister of works, with the posthumous name Yuancian.

s0050.idiomatic: All of them rose to regular office.

s0051.literal: The twelfth son Yang has a separate biography.
s0051.idiomatic: The twelfth son, Yang, has a separate biography.

s0052.literal: Wang Tong, styled Gongda, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
s0052.idiomatic: Wang Tong, styled Gongda, was a native of Linyi in Langye.

s0053.literal: His grandfather Fen was Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil of Liang.
s0053.idiomatic: His grandfather Fen had been left grand master of the golden sigil under Liang.

s0054.literal: His father Lin was Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works.
s0054.idiomatic: His father Lin was left chief clerk in the Ministry of Works.

s0055.literal: Editorial footnote marker 2. Lin, in Qi times married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister Princess of Yixing long, had nine sons, and all became renowned.
s0055.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker 2. Lin, in Qi times, married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess of Yixing long; he had nine sons, all of whom won notice.

s0056.literal: Tong, in Liang times began as National University student, passed the classics examination, and became Secretary and Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
s0056.idiomatic: Under Liang, Tong entered service as a national university student, passed the classics examination, and became secretary and mentor to the heir apparent.

s0057.literal: As the emperor's sister's son he was enfeoffed Marquis of Wuyang ting.
s0057.idiomatic: As kin of the imperial house he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang.

s0058.literal: He rose through Chief Clerk in a princely establishment, Extra-Quota Recorder in a commandery staff, Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent, attendant gentleman in the establishment of the Prince of Luling, Grand General of Cavalry, Editorial footnote marker 3. Chief Clerk in the establishment of He Jingrong of Central Authority, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and was dismissed for an offense.
s0058.idiomatic: He rose through chief clerk in a princely establishment, extra-quota recorder in a commandery staff, chief clerk in the Ministry of Works, household supporter of the heir apparent, attendant gentleman in the Prince of Luling's establishment, [3] chief clerk to He Jingrong of Central Authority, and attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then was dismissed for an offense.

s0059.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Jiangling; Emperor Yuan made him Regular Attendant of the Secretariat and promoted him to Minister of Ceremonials.
s0059.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Jiangling; Emperor Yuan made him regular attendant of the Secretariat and then minister of ceremonials.

s0060.literal: After Jing's rebellion the palace halls within the capital were all burned to ashes; Tong was made concurrent Master of Works in charge of construction, returned to the capital, and solely managed repairs.
s0060.idiomatic: After Jing's rebellion the palaces within the capital had all been burned to ash; Tong was made concurrent master of works for construction, returned to the capital, and alone directed the rebuilding.

s0061.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made Tong Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
s0061.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made Tong director of the Ministry of Personnel.

s0062.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was added Palace Attendant, Director unchanged.
s0062.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaotai (555) he was added palace attendant while keeping the directorship.

s0063.literal: Soon he was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Director of Personnel unchanged.
s0063.idiomatic: Soon he was made right vice director of the Masters of Writing, still heading personnel.

s0064.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was transferred to Left Vice Director, Palace Attendant unchanged.
s0064.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, he was transferred to left vice director, retaining palace attendant.

s0065.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he headed Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
s0065.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded, he headed tutor to the heir apparent.

s0066.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he was General Who Assists the Right and Right Grand Master of the Golden Sigil, with aides and clerks as needed.
s0066.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiankang (566) he was made General Who Assists the Right and right grand master of the golden sigil, with aides and clerks as needed.

s0067.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, his title was changed to General Who Pacifies the Right, and he again headed Grand Arbiter of South Xuzhou.
s0067.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, his title was changed to General Who Pacifies the Right, and he again headed grand arbiter of South Xuzhou.

s0068.literal: In the first year of Taijian he was transferred to Left Grand Master of the Golden Sigil.
s0068.idiomatic: In the first year of Taijian (569) he was transferred to left grand master of the golden sigil.

s0069.literal: In the sixth year he was given Supernumerary Privilege; Palace Attendant, general, Grand Master, and aides unchanged.
s0069.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was given supernumerary privilege; palace attendant, general, grand master, and aides all remained as before.

s0070.literal: Before he took up the appointment he died, aged seventy-two.
s0070.idiomatic: Before he could enter the new office he died, aged seventy-two.

s0071.literal: An edict posthumously restored his offices, posthumous name Cheng, and on the burial day granted one set of martial music.
s0071.idiomatic: An edict restored his offices posthumously, gave him the posthumous name Cheng, and granted one set of martial music on the day of burial.

s0072.literal: Younger brothers Zhi and Gu each have a separate biography.
s0072.idiomatic: His younger brothers Zhi and Gu each have a separate biography.

s0073.literal: Mo, styled Gongji, Editorial footnote marker 4. was Tong's younger brother.
s0073.idiomatic: Mo, styled Gongji, [4] was Tong's younger brother.

s0074.literal: Fine bearing and deportment, broad learning in books and histories, calmly pure and simple, never had profit or desire tug at his heart.
s0074.idiomatic: He had a fine presence, wide reading in history, and a calm, spare manner; profit and desire never touched his mind.

s0075.literal: In Liang he was a National University student in the Book of Changes, scored highest in the archery-and-writing examination, appointed Secretary, Mentor to the Heir Apparent, personal secretary to the Prince of Wuling of Xuanhui, and Records Officer to the Prince of Hedong.
s0075.idiomatic: Under Liang he studied the Book of Changes at the national university, took top marks in the archery-and-writing examination, and served as secretary, mentor to the heir apparent, personal secretary to the Prince of Wuling of Xuanhui, and records officer to the Prince of Hedong.

s0076.literal: When the prince went out to hold Jiangkou, Mo was about to follow to the principality; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang then held selection offices; Mo went to bid Zuan farewell; Zuan admired his presence and said: "Master Wang's talent and standing—how can he wander in an outer princely house?
s0076.idiomatic: When the prince went out to hold Jiangkou, Mo was to accompany him to the fief; Zhang Zuan of Fanyang then controlled appointments. Mo came to take leave of him, and Zuan, struck by his bearing, said, "A man of your talent and station—how can he be left to wander in an outer princely house?

s0077.literal: " He memorialized to make him Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
s0077.idiomatic: " He memorialized to make him grand mentor to the heir apparent.

s0078.literal: He was transferred to Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Left Western Adjutant of the Ministry of Works.
s0078.idiomatic: Mo was transferred to attendant to the heir apparent and left western adjutant in the Ministry of Works.

s0079.literal: He went out as Registrar and Retainer's Assistant of South Xuzhou.
s0079.idiomatic: He went out as registrar and retainer's assistant of South Xuzhou.

s0080.literal: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs; the route passed through Zhufang; Mo greeted him per custom; the Emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; every mountain and river passed, the Emperor inquired; Mo answered each matter with historical precedent.
s0080.idiomatic: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs by way of Zhufang; Mo met him as custom required. The emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; at every hill and stream he asked questions, and Mo answered each with historical precedent.

s0081.literal: He also followed him up Beigu Tower to compose poetry; the diction was clear and canonical; the Emperor greatly praised him.
s0081.idiomatic: He also followed him up Beigu Tower to compose verse; the language was clear and classical, and the emperor praised him warmly.

s0082.literal: At the time the Prince of Hedong was Inspector of Guangzhou; Mo was made Chief Clerk to the Prince of Hedong, Champion, and Administrator of Nanhai.
s0082.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Hedong was inspector of Guangzhou; Mo was made his chief clerk, champion, and administrator of Nanhai.

s0083.literal: The prince reached Lingnan and there greatly plundered; fearing guilt he claimed illness, entrusted the province and returned to court; Mo conducted Guangzhou establishment affairs.
s0083.idiomatic: The prince reached Lingnan and plundered widely; fearing punishment he pleaded illness, handed back the province, and returned to court, leaving Mo to run Guangzhou affairs.

s0084.literal: The Yue region was rich; former governors and magistrates were usually greedy and licentious; Mo alone was known for purity and integrity.
s0084.idiomatic: The Yue country was wealthy, and former governors and magistrates were commonly greedy and unrestrained; Mo alone was known for clean government.

s0085.literal: He entered court as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
s0085.idiomatic: He returned to court as attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

s0086.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled west to Jiangling; Emperor Yuan's provisional regime made him Household Supporter of the Heir Apparent, in charge of the chief minister's records.
s0086.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled west to Jiangling; under Emperor Yuan's provisional regime he was household supporter of the heir apparent, in charge of the chief minister's records.

s0087.literal: He went out as General of Distant Pacification and Administrator of Jinling.
s0087.idiomatic: He went out as General of Distant Pacification and administrator of Jinling.

s0088.literal: After troops and famine the commandery was wasted; Mo's government was pure and simple, and officials and people found ease.
s0088.idiomatic: After war and famine the commandery lay in ruins; Mo governed plainly and simply, and officials and people alike were at ease.

s0089.literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant and promoted to Minister of War.
s0089.idiomatic: He was recalled as palace attendant and promoted to minister of war.

s0090.literal: When Western Wei raided Jiangling, Emperor Yuan summoned the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun, to aid; Mo was left to oversee Xiangzhou.
s0090.idiomatic: When Western Wei attacked Jiangling, Emperor Yuan summoned Xiao Xun, Marquis of Yifeng and inspector of Xiangzhou, to reinforce him; Mo was left to oversee the province.

s0091.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made him Director of the Secretariat.
s0091.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Jing's provisional regime made him director of the Secretariat.

s0092.literal: In the first year of Shaotai he was added Palace Attendant.
s0092.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaotai he was added palace attendant.

s0093.literal: When the Founder was Minister of Works, Mo was concurrently Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
s0093.idiomatic: When the Founder was minister of works, Mo was concurrently his chief clerk.

s0096.literal: [Mo] was concurrently Chief Clerk to the Chancellor, Editorial footnote marker 5. Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat unchanged.
s0096.idiomatic: Mo was concurrently chief clerk to the chancellor, [5] retaining palace attendant and director of the Secretariat.

s0097.literal: At the time Wu suffered disorder and the people were much in want; Mo was made overseer of Wu commandery of Xing.
s0097.idiomatic: Wu was then in turmoil and the people were destitute; Mo was put in charge of Wu commandery of Xing.

s0098.literal: After Xiao Bo was pacified, because Mo had long been in Lingnan with earlier administrative merit, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander over twenty prefectures including Guangzhou, General Who Pacifies the South, General of the Pacification of Yue Central Corps, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
s0098.idiomatic: After Xiao Bo was subdued, because Mo had long served in Lingnan with a record of good rule, he was given the staff, command over twenty prefectures including Guangzhou, the titles General Who Pacifies the South and General of the Pacification of Yue Central Corps, and the post of inspector of Guangzhou.

s0099.literal: Before he set out, he was changed to Inspector of Hengzhou, staff and command unchanged.
s0099.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post he was reassigned to inspector of Hengzhou, with staff and command unchanged.

s0100.literal: Wang Lin held the upper reaches; Heng and Guang wavered; Mo could not reach his post and remained at Dayu Ridge.
s0100.idiomatic: Wang Lin held the upper Yangzi; Heng and Guang were divided in loyalty; Mo could not reach his command and stayed at Dayu Ridge.
